case.composition.title: How the recommendation was composed
case.composition.P1: Escalate to an experienced reviewer: a nonsense value, the mature-deletion rule, or at least two concern questions read yes.
case.composition.P2: Ask for a local check: the edits claim a real-world change and the discussion cites a source.
case.composition.P3: Ask for the source: the edits claim a real-world change.
case.composition.P4: Welcome and tips: the account is new, or the tags or the comment do not look right.
case.composition.P5: No action suggested: every question the table reads is decisive and reassuring.
case.composition.P6: Ask for the source: nothing above applied, so the evidence is not decisive.
case.composition.N1: Possible deliberate damage: a nonsense value, or at least two concern questions read yes.
case.composition.N2: Needs local knowledge: the edits claim a real-world change, or the mature-deletion rule fired.
case.composition.N3: Likely good-faith mistake: the account is new, or the tags or the comment do not look right.
case.composition.N4: Consistent edit: every question the table reads is decisive and reassuring.
case.composition.N5: Needs local knowledge: nothing above applied, so the evidence is not decisive.
case.rules.title: Rules that fired
case.rule.R1: A feature older than a year, or with five or more earlier versions, was deleted. This rules out a looks-consistent lane and a no-action response.
case.rule.R2: The changeset is a mass deletion, a mass modification or a possible import, so a person should look at it.
case.rule.R3: Too little of the changeset could be fetched (a low coverage score or many history gaps), so the lane is Insufficient evidence.
case.rule.R4: An account less than seven days old deleted elements, so a person should look at it.
case.rule.R5: An escalation had no support in the evidence, so it was lowered to a question about the source.
case.rule.R6: The model produced no output, so only the rules apply.
